_comment: Lighthouse budget for three representative page types: homepage, an
Application (Studio) page, and an individual tool page.
Thresholds are measured, not aspirational (PROJECT_LOG.md entry 34). Over
3 runs per URL, seo/accessibility/best-practices showed ZERO run-to-run
variance (e.g. accessibility 0.91, 0.91, 0.91) because they are DOM-based
audits, not timing ones -- which is why they are safe to block on.
performance is 'warn' on purpose. It measured 1.0 locally on every run,
but that was a fast desktop; a shared CI runner's timing varies and this
was NOT verified there. A perf score that fails intermittently teaches
everyone to ignore the whole job, so it reports without blocking until
someone has real runner data to set it from.
accessibility is pinned at 0.90 -- just under the measured 0.91/0.93 -- so
it prevents regression without demanding the existing color-contrast and
unlabeled-file-input fixes, which are application changes (see entry 34).
startServerCommand is `wrangler dev`, not `next start`: the site is a
static export, and `next start` refuses to run against one. It fails in a
way worth knowing about -- it prints 'Ready in 227ms' and *then* errors,
so startServerReadyPattern matches, Lighthouse starts loading pages and
the run fails with connection errors that look like a page problem rather
than a dead server.
The URLs use 127.0.0.1 rather than localhost because wrangler binds IPv4
only, while localhost resolves to ::1 first on some hosts.
